claim: The CAS write-path stage-1 effort targets the backlog item reporting CAS-on-S3 INSERT as approximately 7.6× slower than standard S3.

In the measured 500-partition profile, `ReplicatedMergeTreeSink::finishDelayed` commits partitions serially, the ref-ledger batch size is 1.0, and `CasRefBatchFlushes` equals `CasRefBatchedMutations` at 1026.
Stage 1 is limited to CAS-internal changes plus minimal pool server wiring and has no behavioral seam in MergeTree or generic-Disks code; cross-part `commitPart` concurrency is deferred to stage 2.

`Cas::PartWriteTxn::uploadBlobDetached` must not read or mutate `PartWriteTxn` `build` state, because the transaction is single-writer; it returns a `BlobUploadResult` containing the complete dependency effect and outcome.

`uploadBlobDetached` keeps conditional body/meta operations, freshness transition to `Clean`, condemned-object resurrection, dedup-cache operations, event emission, request accounting, and ProfileEvents inside each upload task so branch ordering is preserved.

All CAS event emission routes through one reentrancy-safe serialized dispatcher, and ledger events are emitted after releasing ledger locks; per-component event locks are rejected because they can deadlock with reentrant sinks.

Condemned-local resurrection uses a byte-weighted semaphore whose weight is the checked header-plus-payload size; a blob heavier than total capacity gets exclusive access after the semaphore drains, and the permit is released after `putOverwrite` and body destruction.

`PartWriteTxn::mergeBlobUploadResults` must prevalidate all results and apply them with build-and-swap or equivalent no-throw replacement so a merge failure leaves the transaction build completely untouched.
Blob fan-out groups pending blobs by `BlobRef`, rejects conflicting declared sizes, launches exactly one task per unique ref, and merges exactly one dependency result per unique ref.

If any blob-upload task fails, the join drains every task and merges no result; publish fails, the precommit is abandoned, staging cleanup follows the existing policy, and successful sibling bodies remain ordinary GC-reclaimable zero-edge debris.

Blob fan-out uses a dedicated server-wide pool disjoint from `getThreadPoolWriter`; the caller only submits and joins, pool size 1 is valid and serializes work, the getter fails if uninitialized, and a configured size of 0 is rejected.
Upload tasks must capture owning or value state, and the callback runner must be scoped so its destructor drains tasks before captured storage is destroyed, including when dispatch throws.

The ref-ledger carve is two-phase: a throwing plan scans `pending` and reserves all capacity without mutation, then a no-throw publish under the same `ref_queue_mutex` pops selected items and moves them into `owned_items`.
The former interleaved ref-ledger carve could lose already-popped items when `seen_refs`, batch, or `owned_items` allocation threw, leaving waiters blocked and callback lifetimes unsafe.
The validation loop reserves `final_ops` and `survivors` before applying an item to `working`, and publishes `working` only after all accumulation operations that may throw have completed.
Normal ref-ledger admission uses `ref_txn_max_ops` 5000 and `kMaxRefBatch` 1000; the former byte-estimate admission and give-back spill are not used.

Each ref-ledger chunk is a complete commit boundary: it allocates a real transaction id, encodes and PUTs the chunk, applies it to `rt->state`, updates tail counters and metrics, completes that chunk's survivors, wakes waiters, and schedules snapshot publication before reseeding the next chunk from live state.

If chunk N fails after earlier chunks committed, chunks before N remain successful and only chunk N plus the unattempted remainder fail; after any committed chunk, later exceptions are contained within the tenure and a leader whose item already succeeded returns that committed result.

Snapshot publication must re-evaluate the accumulated tail or remember and re-fire a pending trigger, because single-flight suppression can otherwise let a publication of chunk 1 hide chunks 2 through N indefinitely.

An item with more than `ref_txn_max_ops` operations fails alone, while removal-class items are exempt from the op cap only when their built operations contain `RemoveNamespace`; `WholeShard` scope alone is not the discriminator.

The normal-class whole-transaction decode cap is 20 MiB, the removal-class byte budget is 64 MiB via `ref_removal_max_bytes`, and normal-class operations have a 4 KiB per-operation cap enforced at admission and decode.

The pre-release CAS policy permits removing `RefOp::payload` and renaming `SetPayload` to `SetPublishedAt` with wire word `set_payload` to `set_published_at` because every existing pool is recreated before release and no old-field decoder tolerance is required.
Streaming ref recovery applies decoded transactions one at a time into a private candidate `RefTableState` and never mutates live `rt.state` until complete recovery is ready.
A vanished selected ref-log object causes candidate discard and a bounded fresh LIST restart, whereas decode or apply corruption discards the candidate and propagates immediately without re-listing.

Recovery publication installs every `RecoveryResult` field atomically under `state_mutex`, sets `recovered` last, and notifies waiters only after state, cleanup markers, snapshot identity, tail accounting, budgets, stale-precommit state, and recovery-seal facts are complete.
Stage 1 adds one server-level CAS upload-pool size setting and rejects an uninitialized or zero-sized pool; non-CAS disks and engines have no behavior change.
Stage 1 intentionally leaves `CasRefBatchFlushes` and `CasRefBatchedMutations` at an average batch size near 1.0; reducing that serial cross-part metric belongs to stage 2.
The PR #2073 sanitizer-abort fix keeps the production `LOGICAL_ERROR` guards unchanged for the GCS conditional dialect and dedup-log null-writer findings; only tests are changed for those findings.
Tests for `LOGICAL_ERROR` guards use `EXPECT_THROW` on release builds and `EXPECT_DEATH` under `DEBUG_OR_SANITIZER_BUILD`, with death suites named using a `DeathTest` suffix.

Constructing `ReadBufferFromMemoryFileBase` with `owns_memory=true` and empty data can pass `nullptr` from `std::string_view::data()` to `memcpy` with length zero, violating the nonnull contract under UBSan.
The empty-file `ReadBufferFromMemoryFileBase` fix is to skip `memcpy` when `data.empty()`; no bytes need copying and the owned buffer must still construct at EOF.

The mount-lease renewal classifier, GCS conditional dialect tests, and dedup-log null-writer tests exposed `LOGICAL_ERROR` construction behavior that aborts debug or sanitizer builds before `catch` can run.

The S41 wide-insert baseline found CAS-on-S3 at 3.0× slower than plain S3, with 87.2% of Real time in S3 network operations, 12.6% in the HEAD-before-PUT gate, and about 77 blob PUTs per part on the wide profile.

Stage 1 reduced the measured CA INSERT from 58.41 seconds to 30.26 seconds, from 3.0× to 1.59× versus plain S3, while CPU/wall increased from 0.375 to 1.075 and the top-thread share fell from 72.3% to 14.5%.

The proposed stage-2 concurrent `commitPart` work was postponed because its upstream and generic-code impact was judged too strong and unpredictable; the research was retained in BACKLOG under `stage2-concurrent-commitpart-postponed`.
Same-pool fetch-by-relink can leave the receiver with a dangling committed manifest if the receiver's `precommitAdd` edge is not durable before the sender's now-`Outdated` part is collected.

A ref-log transaction can become durable before its in-memory apply throws, allowing a later transaction to apply without contiguity checking and a snapshot to label the state with the later transaction id, permanently hiding the earlier transaction from recovery.

If the hidden transaction is a removal, GC can delete blobs that the recovered writer view still references, producing a dangling committed manifest; if it is an addition, GC over-protects blobs; without a covering snapshot, recovery can repeatedly fail with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
The retention-pin design was rejected because it would add a pool-global GC overlay, union folding, removal deferral, and owner-liveness machinery to the most safety-critical component.

The reserved-precommit design was abandoned because it caused state-model sprawl, let a foreign writer bypass `stageManifest` and `adoptEvidence` discipline, and mismatched the `tmp-fetch_<part>` contract.
The ref-lane fix must land before publish-confirm work, and all three post-durable sites must install state without allocation: chunk commit apply, wedge-resolution apply, and wedge construction.

For chunk commit, the candidate is built by copying live state and applying the complete chunk with the real transaction id before PUT; after a committed PUT, the candidate is moved into `rt->state` under `state_mutex` and `DENY_ALLOCATIONS_IN_SCOPE`, then materialized outside the deny region.

`DENY_ALLOCATIONS_IN_SCOPE` covers only the pre-existing candidate move and atomic tail-counter bumps; candidate construction, logging, events, survivor completion, exception creation, notification, and `materializeCommitted` remain outside the deny region.

The apply-pending marker transitions `Clean → ApplyPending` before a durable PUT, returns to `Clean` after successful apply or proven non-durability, and becomes terminal `Poisoned` when apply throws after durability; only fresh recovery clears `Poisoned`.

A `Poisoned` marker is not sufficient protection before the no-throw install fix: without that fix, later transactions could still publish a snapshot hiding a durable missing transaction, so poison must either follow A1 or become a hard per-namespace fence.

`precommitAdd` may take an unowned `ManifestId` only from the transaction that freshly staged it; already-committed idempotence remains a read-only no-op, making exact `ManifestRef` equality an ABA barrier.
Fetch-by-relink follows publish-then-confirm-then-promote: the receiver first durably publishes its own `+1`, then performs one read-only `confirmExactRef`, and promotes only on `yes`.
A confirm token contains `{pool_uuid, server_root_id, root_namespace, ref_name, part_name, ManifestRef}`; `server_root_id` is required because a pool UUID can be shared across server roots.

Gate 0 is only a part-anchored availability filter: it may return a conservative `no` for absent, `Deleting`, or wrong-disk parts, but a `yes` never proves that no removal was initiated and is authorized solely by gate 1.

Authoritative gate 1 takes `ref_queue_mutex`, pins the resident runtime, then takes `state_mutex` as one snapshot; it returns `yes` only for a warm, live, quiescent, unpoisoned table whose committed `ref_name` row exactly matches the token's `ManifestRef` and whose mount fence is live.
Gate 1 returns `unknown` for a cold, recovering, superseded, nonresident, poisoned, wedged, pending, leader-active, or mid-tenure table, and performs no object-store I/O.

A gate-1 `yes` proves the exact transferred manifest was the committed binding at confirmation, no removal was durable or in flight past admission, no durable-but-unapplied transaction existed, and the responder was the live writer; any removal appended afterward is ordered after confirmation.

After a successful confirm, GC cannot delete the referenced blobs before a later removal event because every fold that sees a post-confirm `-1` also sees the durable receiver `+1`, and a straddling fold spares positive in-degree rows.

`PreparedRelink` is a move-only handle that owns the receiver transaction, manifest, target ref, decoded entries, and exact source token; it uses a scope guard to append a durable abort on every non-promote exit.

An unresolved relink abort leaves the ref lane wedged until exact-GET resolution or remount; a landed abort PUT is applied before unwedging, while a never-landing PUT causes retry-later behavior and fail-long over-protection.

The typed relink boundary treats confirm `no`, `unknown`, and transport failure as `SourceProofFailed`: it aborts and throws a locally generated retry-later error rather than returning `false` for same-sender byte fallback.

`MechanismFallbackAllowed` remains the byte fallback for version or cookie mismatch, manifest decode failure, or receiver-side publish or promote conflict; mixed versions degrade to bytes and never to unconfirmed relink.

The new `confirm_ca_ref` interserver action carries the exact token in a second authenticated HTTP request after the relink response is consumed, and responses are `yes`, `no`, or `unknown`; transport errors map to `SourceProofFailed`.

B66b uses a dedicated `allow_ca_relink` capability independent of `try_fetch_shared`; every same-sender byte fallback clears `allow_ca_relink` to prevent recursive relink loops, while legacy `try_zero_copy` behavior remains unchanged.

The fetch-handoff implementation order is pinning test, no-throw ledger install, poison and mint tightening, TLA mini-model, confirm core, B66b recursion brake, and then the test battery; if A1 is deferred, poison must be a hard fence.

The fetch-handoff design does not change GC folding, journal codec, snapshot format, sweeps, orphan protection, or anomaly suppression; every write remains in its owning domain and the ordinary INSERT/merge path is behaviorally unchanged.

S42 allocation-fault validation must distinguish a generic `MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` from exercising the post-PUT apply window by requiring a targeted failpoint or poison-transition counter; otherwise the result is inconclusive.
The S41 workload is a deterministic single-node `MergeTree` INSERT of 10,000,000 rows, 30 mixed-type columns, 500 partitions, and one part per partition, with merges stopped during measurement.
For the S41 baseline, plain S3 took 19.44 seconds and CAS-on-S3 took 58.41 seconds for 500 parts and 3.53 GiB of logical data; CAS issued 119,432 PUTs, 134,400 HEADs, and about 54,360 GETs.

In the CAS S41 trace, S3 PUT/upload response waits consumed 87.2% of Real wall time, HEAD-before-PUT consumed 12.6%, and serialization, hashing, ref-ledger/manifest encoding, and part writing together consumed under 0.2%.

The S41 CAS upload waits were concentrated in one dominant thread holding 72.3% of Real samples; only three threads appeared, CPU-busy time was 37.5% of wall, and `CasRefBatchFlushes` equaled `CasRefBatchedMutations` at 1000 over 500 parts, an average batch size of exactly 1.0.
The CAS path stages every blob locally and then uploads `pending_blobs` in a serial loop while committing parts one at a time, so one thread orchestrates and waits on each PUT or HEAD in turn.
On the fresh-pool S41 insert, `CasBlobHeadFirst` and `CasBlobBodyPutAvoided` were both 26,680, showing that deduplication avoided 26,680 blob-body uploads while still paying the HEADs.
The S41 HEAD-before-PUT gate issued 134,400 HEADs, or 268.8 per part, and accounted for 12.6% of CAS Real wall time; plain S3 issued no HEADs.
The S41 baseline validates parallel blob upload within a part as stage 1 and identifies concurrent `commitPart` dispatch as the larger stage-2 opportunity for cross-part upload concurrency.

The stage-1 implementation plan decomposes the work into 14 tasks: upload-pool wiring, event dispatch, detached upload, exception-safe merge, fan-out, memory cap, carve, caps, removal classification, chunked flush, decode bounds, payload removal, streaming recovery, and closure measurement.

The definitive CA gtest gate for stage 1 is `build_asan/src/unit_tests_dbms --gtest_filter='Cas*:CaLifecycle*:CaWiring*:ContentAddressed*:CountingBackendShape*:RefSnapshotCodec*:RefTableCacheEviction*:RefWriter*'`; the shorter `Cas*:CA*` filter is considered insufficient evidence.
The stage-1 pool setting `content_addressed_blob_upload_pool_size` defaults to 16, rejects 0, and the pool getter throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` before server or test initialization.

`CasEventDispatcher::emit` serializes concurrent delivery, invokes the sink outside its mutex, and queues reentrant emissions for the already-running drain loop instead of recursively acquiring the delivery lock.

`BlobUploadRequest` is a public CAS-owned type containing `BlobRef`, a source descriptor, and `declared_size`; `BlobUploadResult` contains `BlobRef`, the complete `BlobDepRecord`, and one of seven upload outcomes.

`uploadPendingBlobs` uses `ThreadPoolCallbackRunnerLocal` inside the scope owning captured storage, propagates the query `ThreadGroup`, always drains tasks including dispatch throws, and performs no partial merge on failure.

The condemned-upload memory setting `content_addressed_condemned_upload_memory_bytes` defaults to 0, meaning derived capacity of pool size multiplied by 64 MiB; the semaphore releases its permit only after `putOverwrite` returns and the body is destroyed.

The stage-1 carve test seam distinguishes plan allocations (`PlanSeenRefs`, `PlanBatchGrow`, `PlanReserveOwned`) from publish and validation phases, and requires every plan-phase failure to leave already-selected items either retryable or never popped.

Stage-1 ref admission uses a 4096-byte per-op limit checked both during admission and decode, a 20 MiB normal-class decode cap plus writer runtime throw, and a 64 MiB `ref_removal_max_bytes` budget with no op cap for removal-class transactions.

The stage-1 `RefReplayBuilder` owns a private candidate, applies decoded transactions in place, discards it on failure, and returns a complete `RecoveryResult`; vanished objects re-list, while decode or apply corruption fails fast.

A mount-lease renewal mismatch under the keeper's own `(uuid, epoch)` can construct `LOGICAL_ERROR` and abort ASan or debug builds; the intended response is fail-closed uncertainty with a fence and self-remount.

The fence-not-rescue fix has three phases: exhaustive non-aborting classification in `MountLeaseKeeper::onRenewMismatch`, pre-I/O fence-deadline anchoring, and probe-gated writer-epoch re-minting with decommission-aware policy.

The TLA+ model already maps a confirmed renewal mismatch to `localLost` and proves `SupersededWriterMakesNoMutation`; Phase A is therefore an implementation alignment rather than a new model transition.

For a same-uuid, same-epoch, unfenced mount body, `MountLeaseKeeper::onRenewMismatch` throws `ABORTED` with state-uncertainty diagnostics and relies on fencing plus self-remount rather than constructing `LOGICAL_ERROR`.
For a same-uuid body with a different writer epoch, `onRenewMismatch` throws `ABORTED` as the normal superseded fencing outcome and reports `superseded by a newer incarnation`.

A foreign-uuid mount body remains a deliberate `LOGICAL_ERROR`-loud invariant violation because the owner anchor makes foreign claims protocol-unreachable; the classifier does not take over the mount.
If the mount-slot object vanishes during renewal, the keeper throws `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST`, stops renewing, and fails closed without aborting or re-minting.

The CI reproducer for the mount-lease self-race is a `putOverwrite` that applies to backend state and then throws a transient exception, followed by a confirmed mismatch against the stale token; the background loop must fence and invoke `on_lost` without process death.
Both the keeper's wall-clock `confirmed_deadline_ms` and the runtime's boot-clock mutation fence must be anchored at the pre-I/O renewal attempt instant, not at response or acknowledgement time.
The renewal keeper samples separate wall and `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` anchors before I/O, passes the boot anchor to `on_renew_ok`, and computes each deadline as its own attempt-start anchor plus TTL.

`mountWritable` previously armed `bootMsNow() + TTL` after an unbounded `materialization_grace_ms`; if the grace consumed the TTL, a successor could reclaim the slot while the predecessor armed an already-superseded claim.

When materialization grace consumes the claim TTL, startup must perform exactly one fresh conditional lease write before arming the fence, and that write must fail closed if a successor took the slot.

`allocateWriterEpoch` uses `EpochMintPolicy::NormalMount` by default and, on an absent epoch object, requires an authoritative `probeSentinelRaw` result of `KeyAbsent` before minting; `Present`, `ContainerAbsent`, `AccessDenied`, and `Indeterminate` fail closed.
Plain GET absence cannot safely authorize writer-epoch re-minting because it flattens transport or access failures into not-found; lifecycle decisions must use the authoritative probe outcome.

`EpochMintPolicy::DecommissionRecovery` permits re-minting over a surviving mount only when that mount is terminal, refuses a live member with `ABORTED`, and mints `max(1, surviving.writer_epoch + 1)` so the new epoch is distinct.
A decommission path must not blindly bypass the mount-presence guard: minting epoch 1 over a live epoch-1 mount would recreate the forbidden same-pair twin and defeat live-member refusal.
The epoch-presence probe is paid only on the absent-epoch branch; when the epoch object is present, the normal CAS bump does not probe the mount key.
The final mount-lease validation requires a full `Cas*:CA*` gate and must not claim the CAS-s3 stateless lane is green without actually running that lane or explicitly deferring it to CI.

The original same-uuid/same-epoch self-race proposal is superseded by the v2 fence-not-rescue design because its claim that the pair proves the writer's own prior write was refuted by the absent-epoch re-mint hole.

In the reported PR #2073 CI incident, a mount-renewal timeout was followed about ten seconds later by a confirmed mismatch that reached the base `LOGICAL_ERROR` path and aborted the server during exception construction.

`SingleWriterSlot::backgroundLoop` continues after transient renewal failures while the confirmed lease deadline remains safe, but a definite `PreconditionFailed` mismatch always stops the loop and routes to `onRenewFailed` and self-remount recovery.
The former `MountLeaseKeeper::onRenewMismatch` classifier handled GC-fenced same-uuid bodies, different-uuid bodies, and vanished bodies but had no branch for same-uuid, same-epoch, unfenced bodies.

An earlier renewal PUT can land while its client-side timeout loses the acknowledgement, bumping the mount token or sequence; the next retry then presents a stale token and reaches the classifier gap even though the body looks self-owned.
The superseded branch was intentionally out of scope in the first proposal, but v2 later classifies it as normal fencing because a different epoch indicates a distinct remount incarnation.

Adopt-and-continue of the observed mount token was rejected because it violated the contract that `onRenewMismatch` must throw and would require proof that an unwitnessed body is safe to adopt; fence plus self-remount already exists and is exercised.

The two earlier STID 3982-3b48 fixes replaced ordinary vanished or absent-at-release `LOGICAL_ERROR` paths with non-aborting exceptions, establishing the classifier-hardening pattern used by the later fix.
The implemented v2 design rejects rescue of ambiguous renewals: a lease holder that cannot confirm its renewal is treated as not live, fenced, and self-remounted with a fresh epoch.
Same uuid plus same epoch plus an unfenced body does not prove the body came from the current writer, because a vanished epoch object can let a second same-uuid process re-mint the same pair.

Phase A classifies same-uuid/same-epoch/unfenced as `same_epoch_state_uncertain` with `ABORTED`, same-uuid/different-epoch as `superseded` with `ABORTED`, foreign uuid as `LOGICAL_ERROR`, and absent body as `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST`.

The uncertainty exception includes the observed mount-holder identity and the keeper's local sequence, while `MountConflict` carries the observed identity and distinguishes the branch through its `outcome` string; no new ProfileEvent is required.

The conservative fence-not-rescue behavior costs one self-remount cycle for an ambiguous landed renewal, including about 36.5 seconds of fenced writes with default settings; it requires a timed-out-yet-applied conditional PUT and is expected to be rare on healthy backends.

Phase B removes request latency from lease-fence skew by anchoring both deadline domains at attempt start; the keeper uses wall-clock time and the runtime mutation fence uses `CLOCK_BOOTTIME`, so separate anchors are required.

If startup materialization grace consumes the claim TTL, `mountWritable` must redo one fresh conditional claim before arming the write fence; sane grace values shorter than `TTL − safety margin` incur no redo.

On the absent-epoch path, `NormalMount` proceeds only for authoritative `KeyAbsent`, rejects a present mount as `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and fails closed for `ContainerAbsent`, `AccessDenied`, or `Indeterminate` probe outcomes.

`DecommissionRecovery` is used only by `openForDecommission`; it refuses a live surviving mount and mints an epoch distinct from a terminal surviving mount using `max(1, surviving_mount.writer_epoch + 1)`.
The v2 design status records Phases A-C, the TLA+ gate, and addenda as implemented on `cas-gc-rebuild`, with the `Cas*:CA*` gtest gate green; full live CAS-s3 lane validation remains a CI-push task.
The v2 design explicitly leaves body-nonce rescue, coherent-read machinery, resolve-on-ambiguity, and changes to the mount-lease format out of scope; the safety mechanism is fence plus remount.

If both epoch and mount control objects are wiped under a live mount, a same-pair twin can still exist briefly; the residual design relies on the surviving writer fencing on its next beat rather than allowing silently persistent dual writers.

The TLA+ gate adds the authoritative epoch-presence guard, decommission terminal-mount policy, and negative controls showing that removing the guard or blindly minting epoch 1 over a live mount reaches a same-pair two-writer state.
